dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product puts notices in the flow of its content that stay there: a note beside the paragraph it qualifies, a caution above a procedure, the reason a page is not what the reader expects, a summary of what is wrong with a form, a notice at the top of a screen that something changed underneath the person's work. It draws most of them as a quiet tinted block, some as an outline where a fill would weigh on a dense page or vanish on a tinted surface; it shows information, a warning, an error and a success in that status's colors beside the neutral ones; some have a title, some one or two actions, and some can be closed.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a callout reads: its padding, corners and the gaps between its parts; the outlined look's edge; the glyph's size, gap and opacity; the text styles of the title and the body at each size; for each look (tonal, outlined), without a status and in each status (info, warning, error, success), the fill, the title's and the body's colors and the glyph's color; and the close button's variant. The close button is a Tanrei Button with Button's own tokens: the callout names its variant, and on a filled look gives it the body color of its form as its tone.
rules: A callout is part of the content and stays: a note, a caution, the reason for something, a summary of errors. A message that reports what the app just did and then goes is a snackbar; a choice the person must make before going on is a dialog; a word that names a state is a tag.

A notice for a whole page or screen (often called a banner) is a callout the product places above that region's content, usually live and with an action or a close button. It is not another component, and there is no banner look.

Static content is not an alert: leave live off for a callout that is part of what was written. Turn it on only for a callout that appears, or changes, in answer to something the person did or something that happened.
A status is never shown by color alone: the glyph gives it a shape, and the title says it, or statusLabel adds it in words for assistive technology.

Use the four statuses for what they mean everywhere in the system. Advice (a tip) is not a success and a reminder is not a warning: use the default form with a glyph of your own and say the kind in the title.
Tonal is the default. Use outlined where a fill would vanish (on a tinted surface, inside a filled card) or where many callouts sit close together.
A look's tokens end in its name, after the status when there is one: container.color.tonal, error.container.color.tonal.

The actions are the product's own Buttons and links placed in the actions slot; the callout only lays them out. Prefer outlined or text Buttons, whose labels sit on the callout's own fill in every form; at most two.
The body is the product's content. Long-form blocks inside it are prose, at the callout's size and without a measure of their own.

Its close button is a small icon-only Tanrei Button. Re-value comp.callout.close-button.variant in a layer to change it in every callout of a product; on a filled look it is drawn in the body color of the callout's form (a tone), so recoloring the body recolors it too.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a tinted box by hand.

padding-block.$description: Above the first line and below the last block. With the body's text style this puts the first line where a snackbar's is.

padding-inline.$description: Before the glyph or, without one, the text, and after the text where there is no close button.

padding-inline-end-with-close.$description: After the close button: tighter than after text, because the button's own shape already holds its glyph away from the edge.

gap.$description: Between the text and the close button.

shape.$description: The container's corners: the step of a card and of a snackbar, so a block of content reads as one of the page's blocks and not as a control.

color.$description: The fill, per look, without a status.

tonal.$description: The quiet neutral fill, the one a tonal tag without a status draws.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: The outlined look draws no fill: the surface it sits on shows through.

color.$description: The edge of the outlined look, in every status: the one hairline, the color a divider and an outlined tag draw theirs in. Decorative: the glyph and the words carry the meaning. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw this edge apart from its dividers.

size.$description: The glyph's box: one line of the medium body text, so the glyph sits on the first line without pushing it.

gap.$description: Between the glyph and the text after it, as in a snackbar.

opacity.$description: The opacity the glyph is drawn at, applied to the glyph color of the form: a mark beside the text, a little softer than the text, by the amount a snackbar softens its own. The glyph so drawn keeps 3:1 against its container in every form and scheme of the default system.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product softens the glyph beside a notice's text, by one amount for every status, without recoloring it, and may soften it more or less in a block of content than on a floating bar.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: An opacity is a proportion; no dial scales it. sys.state holds the state-layer and disabled opacities, which are other decisions.

color.$description: The glyph's color without a status, per look: the product's own glyph, since the default form draws none by itself.

typescale.$description: The title, per size: the body's size, heavier.

gap.$description: Between the title and the body below it.

typescale.$description: The body's text, per size: the interface's text style at medium, the style for long reading at large, the two sizes prose has.

gap.$description: Between the text and the row of actions below it.

item-gap.$description: Between two actions, along the row and between rows when they wrap.

variant.$description: The Button variant of the close button, an icon-only small Button (CLO-10). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values, the core Button variants; platforms receive the name. On a filled look the Button draws it in the tone of the callout's form (BTN-45).

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product decides once how the close control of its notices stands: a tonal button that reads as a control on the notice's fill, or a bare glyph that leaves the notice to its text.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: Keeps the bare close glyph this preset draws on a notice; the change to a tonal close button is the default system's.

info.$description: The info form: information. The tonal look is the status's quiet container with its paired content color, the fill a snackbar and a tonal tag of the same status draw; the outlined look keeps the surface's colors and shows the status by its glyph alone.

outlined.$description: No fill, as the outlined look without a status.
The surface's text color: a status does not color long text.

tonal.$description: The status glyph, in the status's own color, drawn at icon.opacity.

outlined.$description: The status glyph, in the status's own color, drawn at icon.opacity: the only place an outlined callout shows its status.
